content.text: Try this alternate class file for Fedora 3.2   ...it uses a ConcurrentHashMap instead.
Chris,
Any reason why the switch to ConcurrentHashMap you proposed wasn't made in master? Does this ticket need to be moved against 3.6.1?
Hello,
We currently use Fedora Commons v.3.6.1, and we recently got through this very same problem.
Also, we noticed that it can be worked around by applying the patch explained at:
http://fedora-commons.1317035.n2.nabble.com/fcrepo-user-ConcurrentModificationException-td7351953.html
but apparently this patch has not been included in subsequent releases.
Do you know the reason for this choice? Do you think that we can apply the same patch to our 3.6.1 in order to have it fixed?
Thanks in advance for your response,
Davide Gallina
Davide,
I'm not sure why this hasn't been applied against 3.6.1 yet. I believe you should be able to apply this against 3.6.1.
Dear Frank,
As you may know, we have been delivered with a special version of Fedora (3.6.1-FCREPO-1075) - built on the basis of 3.6.1 and that fixes this particular problem.
Now, I saw that the new Fedora 3.7 is available: is this fix applied on it? I can't find it into the release notes.
Thank you in advance for your response,
Davide
Hola Davide,
Let me ask Ben, who rolled the release and let me come back to you. I thought the pathc would go into 3.7.1 but I'm not sure about that.
https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/commit/60a7c78701a5501784c742ea522f9fdac898c84f
Was included in 3.7.0
No further releases planned for 3.x
While stress testing Fedora, hitting the fieldsearch interface with many simultaneous requests, a ConcurrentModificationException is sometimes thrown.
See related thread:
http://fedora-commons.1317035.n2.nabble.com/fcrepo-user-ConcurrentModificationException-td7351953.html
Reported vs. Fedora 3.2 with Muradora, but appears to be an issue in all Fedora releases up to and including 3.5
